confidence_basis: The public Noel Lab PDF was reviewed for apparatus, sound motion, timing/distance mappings, tactile/response apparatus, trial formula, and reported result pattern. Core audio-tactile parameters needed by the toolkit are explicit; remaining caveats are physical treadmill/optic-flow context, loudspeaker-array interpolation, exact generated noise waveform/seed, motor latency calibration, and controller latency correction.

profile_recreation_assessment.reason: The publication reports white-noise motion, 2 m path, 0.75 m/s speed, five tactile delays, corresponding distances, standing/walking and looming/receding factors, baselines, catches, repetitions, and total trial count. The toolkit can reproduce the runnable audio-tactile schedule and preserve locomotion/optic-flow context as metadata, but it does not physically control treadmill walking, optic flow, or the original two-array speaker apparatus.

source_checks.scope: Methods and results sections covering Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, including apparatus, stimuli, procedure, trial formula, and result interpretation.
Citation and DOI identity check for the Neuropsychologia article.

review_attempts.result: Confirmed white-noise source, 50 dB loudness, two eight-speaker linear arrays, 2 m path, 75 cm/s motion speed, and standing/walking locomotion context.
Confirmed tactile delays T1-T5 = 440, 880, 1330, 1770, and 2220 ms, with looming mapped D5-D1 and receding mapped D1-D5.
Confirmed Locomotion, Sound Direction, and Sound Distance factors, with sound direction and distance randomized within locomotion conditions.
Confirmed 2 Locomotion x 2 Sound Direction x (5 Distances + 2 Baselines + 1 Catch) x 16 = 512 trials per subject.
Confirmed 100 ms chest vibration using Precision MicroDrives model 312-101 motors and right-thumb button responses through a wireless Xbox 360 controller.

Confirmed reported standing near-body facilitation around D1-D2 and walking expansion through D5/166 cm, with receding sounds not showing the same spatial modulation and optic flow alone not explaining the effect.

stimulus_type.evidence_note: The auditory stimulus class and loudness are stated in the apparatus/stimulus description.

source_provenance.value: Original waveform/seed is not supplied; sound was rendered through a physical loudspeaker array.
source_provenance.evidence_note: The profile uses procedural white noise as the minimum reproducible source.

trajectory_count.value: Two sound directions: looming and receding.
trajectory_count.evidence_note: Sound Direction is a task factor.

trajectory_path.value: Sound moved between the participant and a point 2 m away along the forward path.
trajectory_path.evidence_note: The sound source either approached from 2 m or receded to 2 m.

stimulus_duration.value: Motion duration is derived from the 2 m path and 0.75 m/s speed: approximately 2.67 s.
stimulus_duration.evidence_note: Duration follows directly from reported path length and velocity.

auditory_conditions.value: Looming and receding sound direction crossed with standing and walking locomotion.
auditory_conditions.evidence_note: Locomotion and Sound Direction are explicit factors.

gain_envelope.value: 50 dB loudness reported; exact speaker interpolation/gain envelope not supplied.
gain_envelope.evidence_note: Toolkit stores loudness policy as estimated metadata.

renderer_or_apparatus.value: Two uniform linear arrays of eight JBL Control 1 Pro loudspeakers each, driven by an M-Audio FastTrack Ultra 8R interface.
renderer_or_apparatus.evidence_note: Physical renderer details are reported; the toolkit uses its reference renderer proxy.

trial_rows_families.value: Audio-tactile trials, tactile-only baselines at T1/T5, and sound-only catch trials.
trial_rows_families.evidence_note: The 5 distance, 2 baseline, and 1 catch row families are in the trial formula.

condition_intermixing.value: Sound Direction and Sound Distance were randomized trial by trial; Locomotion was blocked/counterbalanced.
condition_intermixing.evidence_note: Randomization details are sufficient but not required for the minimal profile contract.

blocked_or_random_order.value: Standing and walking locomotion conditions were blocked and counterbalanced.
blocked_or_random_order.evidence_note: Toolkit preserves locomotion as row metadata and distributes the exact pool across run blocks.

iti_jitter_policy.value: Inter-trial interval was randomized between 1 and 1.5 s.
iti_jitter_policy.evidence_note: Encoded as an ITI policy string because the runner currently uses its own block timing controls.

response_window.value: Participants responded as fast as possible to vibration; no numeric timeout is reported in the extracted method text.
response_window.evidence_note: The validator uses mouse-click injection on expected response rows.

task_sequence_rules.value: Respond to chest vibration and withhold on sound-only catch trials.
task_sequence_rules.evidence_note: Target and no-go rules are explicit.

tactile_stimulus.value: 100 ms chest vibration from Precision MicroDrives shaftless vibration motors, model 312-101, 3 V, 60 mA, 9000 rpm, 150 Hz, 5 g.
tactile_stimulus.evidence_note: Modality, site, duration, and motor specification are reported.

soa_table.value: T1-T5 = 440, 880, 1330, 1770, and 2220 ms. Receding maps T1-T5 to D1-D5; looming maps T1-T5 to D5-D1.
soa_table.evidence_note: The timing and direction-specific mapping are explicit.

baseline_strategy.value: Tactile-only baseline trials at the first and last tactile delays.
baseline_strategy.evidence_note: Baseline is represented as tactile-only rows at 440 and 2220 ms.

baseline_timing.value: Baseline timings T1 and T5: 440 and 2220 ms.
baseline_timing.evidence_note: Baseline timings are part of the trial formula.

catch_trial_type.value: Sound-only catch trial with no vibration and no response.

repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.value: Each condition row was repeated 16 times.
repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.evidence_note: The trial formula gives x16 repetitions.

baseline_count.value: 128 tactile-only baseline rows per subject: 2 locomotion x 2 sound direction x 2 baseline timings x 16.
baseline_count.evidence_note: Derived directly from the explicit formula.

catch_count.value: 64 sound-only catch rows per subject: 2 locomotion x 2 sound direction x 1 catch x 16.
catch_count.evidence_note: Derived directly from the explicit formula.

block_count.value: The paper reports blocked locomotion/counterbalancing, not a numeric toolkit block count; the runnable profile distributes the exact 512-row pool across eight run blocks.
block_count.evidence_note: Block count is a toolkit packaging choice, not a stimulus-parameter claim.

total_trial_count.evidence_note: The paper states the formula and total.

expected_outcome.standing: Reaction-time facilitation is expected close to the body, around D1-D2.
expected_outcome.walking: Walking expands facilitation through D5, around 166 cm.
expected_outcome.receding: Receding sounds do not show the same space-dependent facilitation pattern.
expected_outcome.optic_flow: Experiment 2 indicates optic flow alone does not account for the walking expansion.

critical_caveats: The toolkit can validate the runnable audio-tactile schedule and output artifacts, not human walking behavior or the scientific RT effect.
Treadmill walking and optic flow are condition metadata in this profile.
The physical dual-speaker-array interpolation is represented by the toolkit's reference renderer and row-level trajectory metadata.
The original white-noise waveform/seed and motor/controller latency corrections are not supplied.
next_manual_action: Use this review as the source contract for noel_2015_walking_full_body_action validation. Do not claim physical treadmill, optic-flow, or loudspeaker-array replication beyond the documented metadata boundary.
